title: Finite algebra trace nondegeneracy detects etaleness
statement: Let K be a field and A a commutative K-algebra finite-dimensional as a K-vector space. The bilinear form (a,b)↦Tr_A/K(ab) is nondegenerate if and only if A is an etale K-algebra. A may be the zero algebra.

proof.text: For nilpotent a, each ab is nilpotent. Algebra.isNilpotent_trace_of_isNilpotent and reduction of K show Tr(ab)=0; left nondegeneracy therefore makes a zero. Install IsReduced A and IsArtinianRing A.

Use IsArtinianRing.equivPi A, restricted to K, to identify A with its finite product of maximal-ideal quotient fields. Fix a factor i. If its trace map were zero, the element corresponding to Pi.single i 1 would pair to zero with all b, by trace_eq_of_algEquiv and the already proved source trace_pi_single. Nondegeneracy makes that element zero, contradicting its i-th coordinate being one.
The traceForm_nondegenerate_tfae field theorem converts nonzero trace on each factor to separability. Algebra.Etale.iff_exists_algEquiv_prod then proves the algebra etale.

Conversely install Algebra.Etale K A and apply the already proved source Algebra.Etale.exists_trace_mul_ne_zero to a hypothetical nonzero element in either radical. The right-radical case uses commutativity. This proves both halves of Nondegenerate, including the zero-algebra case.

    (traceForm K A).Nondegenerate ↔ Etale K A
